items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: After my band broke up, you know, the blind Freddie got me with him, you know, with Amos Riley. Then I had Amos Riley with us on the car in the Arlene Creole Jazz Band. Had him with us in there.

ctx.x: What, by that? He used to work with Mamie Smith too, didn't he?

With who? Mamie Smith. Who, me? No, Robert Taylor. Used to work with Amos? Mamie Smith. Yeah, yeah, he left there with her, yeah. That's right. Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's where he left after we dropped out. We was with him then, with Robert Taylor, you know. What part of town was he from? The people and mother, they wanted to go. You say, what part of town was Robert Taylor from, uptown or downtown? He was from out front, out front of town. Well, we'll ask Dave Bailey about him, him being other one of them.…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Oh, Amos Riley, I used to play with him too.

ctx.x: See, a long time ago when we were playing music, we could play in a big hole like that, we'd play about two pieces and take about fifteen minutes, you know, intermission. And some of them, good bands, take a half an hour, you know. But now you get there, you gotta play. That's my house wasn't at it. Just like a Jitney dance. That's the way to play it. I tell you that on them now. We didn't ask him about Amos Riley. The sign? Amos Riley. Oh, Amos Riley, I used to play with him too. He did, he been to him.
